question: You are designing a notification system that sends push, email and SMS for every order event. Which component should sit between the order service and the delivery workers?
context: Order events arrive in bursts (thousands per minute during sales). Each channel has a different rate limit and provider outages happen weekly. Losing a notification is acceptable only if it is retried later.

options.label: WebSocket connection to each worker
options.why: WebSocket is for pushing to connected clients in real time. It offers no buffering or durability — a worker outage would drop events.

options.label: A message queue / event log
options.why: A queue absorbs bursts, lets each channel consume at its own rate, retries failures and parks poison messages in a dead-letter queue. This is exactly the decoupling the requirements ask for.

options.label: Direct PostgreSQL polling by workers
options.why: Polling a table works at small scale but becomes a hot-spot: locking, wasted queries and no natural back-pressure. Use the database as the source of truth and publish via an outbox instead.

options.label: Redis GET/SET shared state
options.why: Redis is great for counters and rate-limit windows here, but plain keys are not a durable work queue. Redis Streams could work; a dedicated broker is the safer default.
